page.title: Apeirophobia Roblox Quiz: 15 Questions on Chapter 1 Levels
page.description_md: Think you know Apeirophobia's original Chapter 1? It covers Levels 0–16, and each attempt draws 15 random questions: five easy, five medium and five hard. See how well you remember the routes, puzzles and entity rules.
page.seo_description: Test your knowledge of Roblox Apeirophobia's original Chapter 1 across Levels 0 to 16, from route markers to the ending. Each attempt gets 15 random questions.

easy.question: Which route leads out of Level 0?

options.text: A ladder into a wall vent.
A ladder through a ceiling opening.
A ladder over a dividing wall.
A ladder through a window.

easy.question: How many valves must you turn to open the Level 1 gate?

options.text: Four.
Five.
Six.
Seven.

easy.question: What takes you to Level 3 at the end of Level 2's main path?

options.text: Returning to the starting room.
Searching the kitchen drawers.
Jumping into the giant pit.
Exploring the bathroom.

easy.question: What should you follow when you are near Level 5's glowing purple exit portal?

options.text: The loudest whistle nearby.
The nearest footsteps.
The quietest passage.
The strange noises it makes.

easy.question: What do you enter to finish the chase in Level 6?

options.text: A glowing door.
A wall vent.
A locker.
A stairwell.

easy.question: Which light sequence leads toward the exit vent in Level 8?

options.text: Red, then green.
Green, then red.
Green, then blue.
Red, then blue.

easy.question: In Level 9's New Objective route, which markers identify the pool leading to Level 10?

options.text: Arrows pointing to it and a green light above it.
No arrows and an orange light above it.
Arrows pointing to it and an orange light above it.
No arrows and a green light above it.

easy.question: In Level 10, what do you use to unlock the correct corner door and reach Level 11?

options.text: A key found at the stop sign.
A switch beside a street lamp.
A code found on a locker.
A key found on a locker.

easy.question: In Level 12, how many paintings must you place correctly on the rack to open the exit?

options.text: Three.
Two.
Four.
Five.

easy.question: Which objectives must you complete in Level 13 before entering the theater exit?

options.text: Three Star Buttons, then five Partypooper Plushies.
Five Star Buttons, then three Partypooper Plushies.
Five Star Buttons, then five Partypooper Plushies.
Three Star Buttons, then three Partypooper Plushies.

easy.question: After opening the electric door in Level 14, which letter do you enter at the computer to open the exit gate?

options.text: x.
n.
y.
q.

easy.question: In Level 15's island facility, which floor has the dip leading to Level 16?

options.text: The first floor.
The second floor.
The fourth floor.
The third floor.

medium.question: What opens the first gate and then the exit door in Level 3?

options.text: Three cabinet keys, then all the second-area buttons.
Two cabinet keys, then all the second-area buttons.
Three cabinet keys, then only one second-area button.
Three cabinet keys, then all the second-area lockers.

medium.question: How do you recover stamina while moving through the chase in Level 6?

options.text: Hold sprint continuously between obstacles.
Walk briefly between bursts of running.
Keep sprint held while jumping between obstacles.
Keep sprint held while sliding through obstacles.

medium.question: Which numbers should you try at Level 7's later keypad in the shelf room?

options.text: The output from the first computer.
The sample number on the computer's note.
The candidate codes in the shelf-room book.
The numbers in the color-priority table.

medium.question: In Level 11, how do you use the crowbar to reach the computer?

options.text: Use it on the color keypad.
Use it on the main gate.
Use it on the computer itself.
Remove the planks from the computer-room door.

medium.question: Which key sequence lets you continue toward the final button gate in Level 11's second area?

options.text: The first key opens a gate; the second opens a door.
The first key opens a door; the second opens a gate.
The first key opens a gate; the second opens another gate.
The first key opens a door; the second opens another door.

medium.question: What confirms that a painting is in the right place in Level 12?

options.text: A sound plays and the room becomes greener.
A sound plays and the room becomes redder.
No sound plays and the room becomes redder.
No sound plays and the room becomes greener.

medium.question: Which tool order opens Level 14's electric box and then cuts its wires?

options.text: Bolt Cutters, then Screwdriver.
Screwdriver, then Crowbar.
Screwdriver, then Bolt Cutters.
Crowbar, then Bolt Cutters.

medium.question: Which electrical panels must you activate to advance from the first two floors of Level 15's island facility?

options.text: Every panel on each floor.
Only faulty panels on each floor.
No panels on either floor.
One working panel on each floor.

medium.question: When the lifeboat engine stalls in Level 15, how do you use its repair prompt?

options.text: Repeatedly press E on PC or repeatedly tap the mobile prompt.
Hold E on PC or hold the mobile prompt.
Press E once on PC or tap the mobile prompt once.
Wait for sailing to resume before using either prompt.

medium.question: After either of the first two required item pickups in Level 16, where do the arrows point?

options.text: Toward the item just collected.
Toward the next required item.
Toward the nearest entity.
Toward the level's starting point.

medium.question: Which route leads through Level 4 to Level 5?

options.text: Hallways, maze, stairs, white glitching portal.
Stairs, hallways, maze, white glitching portal.
Hallways, stairs, maze, white glitching portal.
Maze, hallways, stairs, white glitching portal.

medium.question: Which actions match the repeating obstacles in Level 6?

options.text: Sliding, standing still and using open doors.
Crouching, standing still and using closed doors.
Sliding, standing still and using closed doors.
Sliding, crouching and using open doors.

medium.question: What should you do when your screen shakes because the Hound is close in Level 3?

options.text: Stay crouched and still, with lockers and drawers shut.
Walk crouched while opening lockers and drawers.
Stand still while opening lockers and drawers.
Sprint past while leaving lockers and drawers shut.

medium.question: Which sense does the Hound use to detect players in Level 3?

options.text: Sight, without hearing.
Hearing, without sight.
Both hearing and sight.
Neither hearing nor sight.

hard.question: How do you build the input for Level 7's first color-code computer?

options.text: Put each color's number before its count; arrange the pairs by priority.
Put each color's count before its color number; arrange the pairs in reverse priority.
Put each color's number before its count; arrange the pairs in reverse priority.
Put each color's count before its color number; arrange the pairs by priority.

hard.question: Which entity does the Cameraman alert with its screech and screen-blurring blue shockwaves in Level 0?

options.text: The Hound.
The Starfish.
The Howler.
The Skin Stealer.

hard.question: In Level 1 multiplayer, what can a teammate do from a safe spot to help keep the Starfish nearby?

options.text: Keep a flashlight aimed at it.
Whistle repeatedly.
Keep a camera aimed at it.
Stay silent beside it.

hard.question: How does crouch-walking through the Hound in Level 3 differ between Normal and Nightmare Mode?

options.text: It is safe in Normal but unsafe in Nightmare.
It is unsafe in Normal but safe in Nightmare.
It is safe in both modes.
It is unsafe in both modes.

hard.question: Which pair of traits fits a Skin Walker disguised as a player in Level 5?

options.text: No glowing white eyes; a copied held flashlight or camera.
Glowing white eyes; a copied held flashlight or camera.
No glowing white eyes; no copied held flashlight or camera.
Glowing white eyes; no copied held flashlight or camera.

hard.question: What can vary between runs and change the combination for Level 7's first computer?

options.text: The color numbers printed on the computer.
The color priorities printed on the computer.
The number of gems of each color.
The number of digits in each shelf-room book code.

hard.question: In Level 11, which direction do you read the gem colors to get the color-keypad sequence?

options.text: Left to right.
Right to left.
Alphabetically by color name.
In the order you first notice the gems.

hard.question: After a Stalker scare starts the alarm in Level 14, what must you do with the levers to survive its next scare?

options.text: Flip all three levers.
Flip only one lever.
Flip only two levers.
Leave all three levers untouched.

hard.question: In Level 14, what can trigger a Stalker jumpscare?

options.text: Your camera must face it even if your avatar already does.
Your avatar and camera must both face it at once.
Neither avatar nor camera direction affects its jumpscares.
Your avatar can trigger it while your camera points down.

hard.question: After you successfully finish the Kameloha encounter in Level 15, how long does it leave you alone?

options.text: Only until sailing resumes.
Only until the boat reaches the island.
For the rest of the exploration.
Only until the island facility's first floor lights up.

hard.question: In Level 16, wall strikes have sound cues and the count eventually resets. How many strikes send the Deformed Howler berserk before that reset?

options.text: One.
Three.
Two.
Four.

hard.question: After the Deformed Howler reaches the Bear Trap in Level 16, which sequence is shown in the ending cutscene?

options.text: The lever lowers the cage, gasoline is poured, then a match burns the entity.
Gasoline is poured, a match burns the entity, then the lever lowers the cage.
A match burns the entity, the lever lowers the cage, then gasoline is poured.
The lever lowers the cage, a match burns the entity, then gasoline is poured.
